start: actual New Game directly into the morning; no MQ01/MQ02 progress, actor positions or household receipts seeded
input: real walking, animated doors, proximity conversations, E and Space key events, explicit choices

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Cael? Breakfast’s ready.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *sleepily* All right. I’m coming.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Did I wake you?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Yes.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Oh. I thought I heard you moving.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: That was me trying to get comfortable.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: *a small laugh* Well, get uncomfortable. Mother’s already sent me up once.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Give me a minute.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I’ll be downstairs.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Good morning, Caelan. There’s bread beside your brother. Help yourself.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Morning. Sorry—I didn’t mean to sleep so late.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: You haven’t missed anything. Sit down.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Except the courtyard.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: You’ve finished?

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Most of it. There are still the tables to move.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’ll help you with those.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Good. I wasn’t going to try them on my own.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Do you want the clean cups back on the shelf, Mother?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Leave them by the hearth until they're dry.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I could wipe the table while they’re there.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Yes, that would help. Finish your breakfast first.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: And when we’re finished, could I go over to Mira’s?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: What are you working on?

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Nothing yet. I want to ask her about the arm brace. I can follow each linkage on its own, but I can’t work out how they help her lift without getting in the way of her hand.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: You could ask her to slow him down.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I did. She started explaining, and then someone brought her a broken hinge.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: She’ll be busy today. Ask whether she has time before you settle in.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I will.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Will you need me all afternoon?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: I need some help this morning. What did you have in mind?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I wanted to practise my magicks. Down by the brook, perhaps.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: You had your book out last night.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I know.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I wasn’t complaining.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *a little embarrassed* No. I just keep going back to the same part.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Is there something in it you don’t understand?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: It makes sense when I read it. Then I try, and I can’t tell whether I’ve misunderstood something or whether I simply need more practice.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Would you like someone with you?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: For now, I’d rather try on my own.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: All right. We’ll leave you some time this afternoon.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Thank you.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: You can leave the table to me. I can wipe it down.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: All right.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Eat another piece before you go, both of you. There’s plenty to do today; I expect we’ll all forget to stop for lunch.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I won’t.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Then remind the rest of us.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Here, Mother.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Thank you.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: When you’ve finished, come and see me. There are a few things I’d like taken into the village.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: We’ll come over.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Caelan, could you take these into the village for me? I promised to call on a few people, and I’m going to be needed here.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Yes. Who are we going to?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Halden first. Take the upper bridge to his cottage, just south of the mill. This is the medicine he asked for.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Are his hands troubling him again?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: They were when I saw him. He’s still trying to finish the flour orders before his hands get too stiff.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: We can help with the carrying while we’re there.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Please ask him. He may be more willing to let you help if he’s the one telling you where everything goes.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: He’ll tell us that anyway.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: *a small smile* Quite possibly.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: There’s bread and lamp oil for Elira, too. She was running low on oil for her lantern.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: At home?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: She should be. Her cottage by the southern bridge. If she wants company, stay a little.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: And these are for the Venns, up on the eastern terrace. Their little one’s still recovering.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Still not well enough to come outside?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: I haven’t heard. Ask how this morning has been. They’ve hardly had a chance to think about anything beyond the next meal and the next bit of sleep.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Do they need anything else?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: They may. Let them tell you.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: We’ll start with Halden.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Thank you. Then Elira and the Venns in whichever order suits you.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Am I coming for all three?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Come back after Halden. You and I can get those courtyard tables into place.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I said I’d help with those.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: We can manage. You’ve got the other visits.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: All right. Take the smaller bundle, then. I’ll carry the rest.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Ready.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Nearly there. This fitting has other ideas.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: Morning, you two. Mind that sack by the door.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Serene sent your medicine.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: Ah. Thank you. I meant to go and fetch it.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: She said your hands were hurting.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: They are. Particularly when people keep asking me to tell them about it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Would moving these help?

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: It would. I need the doorway clear before I bring any more flour through.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Where do you want them?

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: On the dry pallet by the north wall. Three sacks. Keep them off the floor.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: There’s more waiting at the mill?

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: There are flour orders waiting, and people need time to bake. I’d like to get it done.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I’ll take the middle one.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Let me—

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I can carry it. Just help me get it settled.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: All right. We’ll lift it together.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: Keep it close once you’ve got it. And put it down if you need to. There’s no prize for getting there without stopping.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: That’s much better. I can get through here again.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Are they far enough back?

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: Yes. Leave them there.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: You’ve still got a lot to do.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: I have. But I can manage the mill without carrying everything in and out as well.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: We can tell Serene you need another pair of hands.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: For the carrying, perhaps. Tell her I asked, before she decides I need someone watching me all day.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’ll tell her.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: And thank you. Both of you.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: The wheel’s been making an awkward noise, too. I’ll have to look at it.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Would Mira know what it is?

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: She might. She learned her way around that mill working with me. These days she notices things I’ve walked past twice.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Have you asked her?

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: Not yet. She’s got people coming to her workshop with their own repairs.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: She’d probably rather hear about it before something breaks.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: *rubs his hand* Yes. I suppose she would.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I’d better get back. Mother will be waiting to move the tables.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’ve still got Elira by the southern bridge and the Venns on the eastern terrace.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: You don’t have to hurry back for us.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I wasn’t going to hurry.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: You were about to tell me to wait for you.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *after a pause* I was going to say I’d help when I got back.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: We’ll leave you something if there’s anything left.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: All right. See you later.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: Caelan. Come in—there’s room, if you can get past the washing.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’ve brought bread and lamp oil from Serene.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: Oh, good. I was trying to remember whether I had enough oil left.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: For your lantern?

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: That, and for seeing what I’m doing tonight. I keep finding one more thing that needs attention.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: What are you working on?

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: My lantern, once I get it down. I put it on that shelf to keep it safe. Now I can’t reach it safely myself.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I can fetch it.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: Would you? The stool’s underneath. Bring it over to the table when you’ve got it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Is the handle secure?

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: It should be, but take it by the bottom as well. I’d rather you didn’t find out halfway down.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: There. Now I can see what needs cleaning.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: The frame’s still sound.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: It’s lasted well. My husband was very particular about putting it away properly. I used to think he made a performance of it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: You’ve kept doing it.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: Yes. Apparently I was listening.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: I like to light it while I sit by the window.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Did he keep it there?

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: Beside his chair. He’d polish the brass until I could see myself in it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *a small smile* Every evening?

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: Whenever he found a mark. He’d hold it up and ask whether I could still see one.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: Sometimes I still turn to tell him he’s missed a spot.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: *after a moment* It could use a little work now.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I know. I wasn’t sure what to say.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: You don’t have to say anything. You’ve brought my lantern down. Stay a minute while I have a look at it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Shall I tell Serene you’ve got everything you need?

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: Yes, please. And thank her for the bread and oil.

pages.speaker: elira
pages.text: Come and find me when you’ve finished helping everyone else.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I will.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: Hello, Caelan. Come in quietly, would you? We’ve finally had a little sleep.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Of course. Serene asked me to bring these.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: Thank you. I meant to get down to Serene’s house yesterday.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: How has this morning been?

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: Better. A little food stayed down, and there hasn’t been so much restlessness.

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: We both managed to sit down for a while.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: Until you went out to the plot.

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: I thought I could get the watering finished before it got warm.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Did something happen?

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: The irrigation gate’s jammed. There’s plenty of water in the brook, but hardly any getting through to the far end of our plot.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: Can it wait?

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: Not all day. I’ve been carrying buckets over, but I can’t keep doing that.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I could look at the gate while I’m here.

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: Would you? It’s just east of the cottage. Check the pin at the side, and the channel below the board.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: The tools are in the box. Borrow what you need.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’ll come back and tell you how I get on.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: The pin’s wedged crooked. The water’s pressing the board against it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: There are twigs caught underneath as well. Even if I free the pin, I’ll need to clear those.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: The mallet should help with the pin. Or I could try pushing the water back for a moment—just enough to take the pressure off.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Come on…

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *quietly* Nothing. I’ll get the tools.

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: It’s reaching the far end now. I saw it coming through.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: The pin was caught at an angle. I set it straight and cleared what was under the board.

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: Thank you. I’d have spent the rest of the morning hauling water.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: Then you can spend some of it in here.

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: Yes. I can.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Does it catch like that often?

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: Often enough that I keep thinking about a pump. They’ve got them in the capital that could do this without all the lifting.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: We’d still have to buy it. And get it repaired when something went wrong.

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: I know. I’m not ordering one. I’d just like to get the watering done without losing half a day to it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Would you want Mira to look at the gate?

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: If it catches again, I’ll ask her. For now, you’ve got it working.

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: Please tell Serene we’re grateful. And that this morning’s been better.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I will. Will you let Serene know if there’s anything else you need?

pages.speaker: venn_mother
pages.text: We will. She’s done plenty for us already.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: All right. I’ll let you have some quiet.

pages.speaker: venn_father
pages.text: Thank you, Caelan.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Caelan, can you look at this?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: What's wrong?

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: It turns most of the way, then it sticks. I can't see what's catching.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Is the pin bent?

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I thought so, but it looks straight.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Have you shown Mira?

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Not yet. I wanted to get it working myself.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: You can still ask her.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: I know. I will if I can't find it.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Hello, Caelan. How did you get on?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Everyone has their supplies. Halden asked whether someone could help with the carrying while he finishes the flour orders.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: He asked?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: He wanted me to make sure you knew that.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: *smiles* I’ll remember. Did the medicine reach him?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Yes. We moved the three sacks out of his doorway as well.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Good. I’ll speak to him about the rest.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Elira’s lantern is down on her table. She wants to clean it this afternoon.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: I thought she might. Was she pleased to have it down?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Yes. She asked me to stay for a little while.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: I’m glad you could.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: And the Venns said this morning’s been better. Their little one’s kept some food down.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Oh, that is good.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Their irrigation gate was jammed. I repaired it while I was there.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Is it working properly now?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: The water’s reaching the far end again. Mr. Venn said that was what he needed.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *hesitates* I tried a spell on it first. I thought I could push the water back while I freed the pin.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: How did it go?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: It didn’t move. I ended up using the tools.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Do you want to tell me about it?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Later, perhaps.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: All right.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Thank you for going round. I’ll follow up with them.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Is there anything else you need before I go?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Nothing that needs you now. Take the time you asked for this morning.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’ll go down to the brook, then.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: Serene? Is Caelan still here?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’m here. What’s happened?

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: The wheel’s stopped. I went back to the mill and there wasn’t enough water coming through to turn it.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Have you been along the channel?

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: As far as the bank. I couldn’t see what was holding it up. Mira needs to look at it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’ll find her.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: Could you help her, too? There may be something to clear, and I’m not much use for that today.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Caelan, you were just going out—

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I can practise later. I’ll go with her.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: *with relief* Thank you. There’s still grain waiting, and people need their flour before they can start baking.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Try her workbench outside the workshop, before the upper bridge. She should be there.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’ll tell her what you’ve seen.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: I’ll head back to the mill. You can find me there.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Keep to the bank until you know what’s wrong, Caelan.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: We will.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Halden’s mill has stopped. He came to the house looking for help.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Stopped completely?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: He said there wasn’t enough water reaching the wheel. He’s been along the bank, but he couldn’t see what was holding it up.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: All right. I’ll come.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: He also asked whether I could help you.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Good. We may need another pair of hands.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Nothing’s caught between the paddles. The axle looks seated, too.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: It is. Look along the supports—nothing’s moved there.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: So the wheel itself might be all right.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: I think it is. Let’s see what’s reaching it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: The brook’s still flowing. It’s only this channel that’s low.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Which means we follow it back to the intake.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: The north road?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Yes. Back over the upper bridge, then past the steps by Serene’s house. The intake’s along the river trail outside the village.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: The wheel’s sound, but it isn’t getting enough water. We’ll follow the millrace back to its intake.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Back over the upper bridge, then north past the steps by Serene’s house.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: That’s right. Take the road out of the village. The intake’s along the river trail.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Keep close once we’re out there. Animals come down to the water, and some of them won’t move aside for us.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Is that why you fitted the arm rig?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Yes. The brace helps me steady the emitter, and I can still use my hand. Let’s hope all we need are the tools.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: All right.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: And leave the sword sheathed while we’re walking. We’ll want our footing on that bank.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: The intake is beyond the bend in the north trail. Stay close—we’ll keep an eye on the riverbank together.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: That tree’s down across the water.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Look at the trunk. Something’s torn into it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Mira. Beyond it.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: I see it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: It brought that down?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: With tusks that size… It must have. A limb could easily have washed into the intake.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: It’s coming this way.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Caelan, back towards me. Slowly.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Caelan. Are you hurt?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *steadies his breathing* Give me a moment.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: All right.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I thought I’d be able to use it.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: You did use it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I couldn’t make the water work. I just kept pushing until something else came through.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Then we’ll look at that somewhere quieter. Right now, I want to know whether you can walk comfortably.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Yes. I can.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Good. Keep it sheathed while we’re working. The intake’s just ahead.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *points to the limb* There. That limb’s wedged across the screen.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: A fresh break, just like the tree by the path. That’s where it came from. Look how the water’s pressing it into the bars.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: *disengages the brace’s powered supports* I’ll leave the joints free for the tools.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: We won’t pull it clear like that.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: No. We’ll take the pressure off first.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: And the catch?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Under the water in that little stone recess. We’ll deal with it once the intake’s isolated.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Tell me where you need me.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: I’ll set the bypass below the screen. Keep clear while I turn it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Here?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: *checks Caelan is clear* That’s fine. Give me a moment.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: That’s taken the main flow off it. There’s still water sitting around the catch.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: It can’t fill again while the bypass is open?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: No. There’s only what’s trapped there.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I want to try moving it into the drain.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: With the blade?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Yes. Just this pocket.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: All right. I’ll stand clear.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *a small, surprised laugh* There. That went where I wanted it.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: And I can see the catch now.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: It felt different. I could keep track of it.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: You had time to do that here.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I’d like to try it again.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: When we’re back. I’d like to see it properly, too.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I wish I’d had this when I was working on the Venns’ gate.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Was the water still flowing against it?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Yes. I was trying to hold it back.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: That’s a much heavier job. We’ve stopped anything feeding this pocket.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I know. I still wanted to manage it.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Then show me what you were trying when we’ve got some time. For now, you’ve cleared what I needed.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: I can release the catch now. Take the rope.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Ready.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Keep the limb clear of the bars when I lift the screen.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Tell me when.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Now.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Hold it there… Good. You can let go.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: The water’s coming through.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: I’ll collect the tools and secure the brace. Then we’ll check the wheel.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Mira?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Yes?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Thank you for bringing it out today.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: I’m glad I did.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I want to spend some time learning it. Without something trying to knock me over.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Come by the workshop when you’re ready. Bring your book.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Let’s get back to the wheel and check it’s taking the load. Then we can give Halden some good news.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: I’ll leave the checking to you and Mira. There’s still grain waiting to be milled.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: I’ll leave the checking to you and Mira. There’s still grain waiting to be milled.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: I’ll leave the checking to you and Mira. There’s still grain waiting to be milled.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: I’ll leave the checking to you and Mira. There’s still grain waiting to be milled.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: I’ll leave the checking to you and Mira. There’s still grain waiting to be milled.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: *smiles* It’s turning.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Steadily, too. The wheel’s taking the load again.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Do we need to check anything else?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: That’s enough. Let’s tell Halden what was caught.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: There you are. I heard the wheel start.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: A limb was jammed across the intake screen. We cleared it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: The wheel itself was all right.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: Good. Was there much damage up there?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: There was a ridgeback tusker by the path. It must have brought the tree down.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: *his expression changes* You ran into it?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: We got past it together.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: It’s gone. But the bank’s torn up—warn anyone carrying loads along there.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: I will. Are you both all right?

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Yes.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: Sit down if you need to. The flour can wait another few minutes.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: We’re all right. I think I’d rather hear it running for a bit.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: So would I.

pages.speaker: halden
pages.text: *after a moment* Thank you, both of you. People can get their flour again.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I should get back home.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: I thought you were going down to the brook.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: I was. But I said I’d help Mother this morning. There’s still time to see what she needs.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: All right. I need to get these tools back before someone brings me another repair.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: See you later.

pages.speaker: mira
pages.text: Bring your book when you come.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: There you are. How’s the mill?

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Turning again. There was a limb caught across the intake. Mira and I cleared it.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Good. Halden must be relieved.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: He stood listening to it for a while.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: *smiles* I can imagine.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Is there anything left to do here? I said I’d help this morning.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: The table's clean. Can you bring over the cups?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: You could bring those clean ones over, if you have a moment.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Yep, on it.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Are these the clean ones?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Yes. Three beside the jug, please. The rest can go on the shelf.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: This one's still warm.

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: It was nearest the hearth. I left them there to dry.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: Do I get the chipped one?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Only if you choose it, Tomas.

pages.speaker: tomas
pages.text: *relieved* I'll take the other one.

pages.speaker: caelan
pages.text: Is this close enough?

pages.speaker: serene
pages.text: Yes. Thank you, love.
